english.title: Fail to notify the Secretary of State of transfer of deactivated firearm
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) transferred the deactivated firearm to another person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) and failed to give notice of the transfer to the Secretary of State

(A)_[before the transfer took place or as soon as reasonably practicable after the transfer]_
(B)_[describing the deactivated firearm by giving, if known, the make, calibre and serial number]_
(C)_[stating the name and address of the person giving notice or to whom the deactivated firearm has been or will be transferred]_
(D)_[as required by published postal or electronic means]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 2(1) and (4) of the Firearms Regulations 2019.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a person in possession of a deactivated firearm
transferred the firearm to another person AND
before the transfer took place OR
as soon as reasonably practicable after the transfer
failed to give notice of transfer to the Secretary of State

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) PLEASE NOTE: This offence is revoked as of 4th March 2026. However, following the savings provisions within regulation 5 of the Firearms (Revocation, Consequential Amendment and Saving Provision) Regulations 2026 an offence may still be committed after this date.

(ii) The Secretary of State will be deemed to have been notified when notice has been given in line with regulation 2(2).
